title: Add an NVLink Engram fetch for single-node runs without NCCL GIN
body:
## Summary

DeepSeek-V4.1 cannot currently run on a node where **NCCL GIN (GPU-initiated RDMA) is unavailable**, even on a single node with all GPUs on NVLink. Examples:

- cloud single-node GPU instances without RDMA;
- development or lab nodes whose compute NICs are not cabled or are disabled;
- hosts whose NIC, firmware or driver setup does not support GDAKI.

This PR adds an opt-in NVLink-only path for the Engram fetch so these nodes can run the model.

## Why Engram is the blocker

`deep_ep.EngramBuffer.fetch` is implemented only on top of GIN. `engram_fetch.cuh` issues `comm::NCCLGin` gets even when `num_rdma_ranks == 1`, because the shards live in host memory owned by other ranks. Without GIN:

- by default, `EngramBuffer` creation fails with `GIN: DevComm setup failed on all available backends`;
- with `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`, the first forward (the profile run) hits `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in the Engram fetch kernel. DeepEP's own `tests/engram/test_engram.py` fails the same way.

Everything else in DeepInfer already works over NVLink in this setting. With `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`, DeepEP `test_barrier.py` and `test_ep.py` (with `--allow-hybrid-mode 0`) and DeepGEMM `test_mega_moe.py` all pass.

## Changes

The default behavior is unchanged: when the flag is off, DeepEP's `EngramBuffer` is used exactly as before.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `deepinfer/model_executor/parallel_utils/engram_nvlink.py` | **New.** `NVLinkEngramBuffer`, a drop-in for the `write` / `fetch` / `destroy` subset used by `EngramRuntime` |
| `deepinfer/environ.py` | `DEEPINFER_ENGRAM_NVLINK_FETCH`; when unset it follows `EP_DISABLE_GIN` |
| `deepinfer/model_executor/parallel_utils/userbuffer.py` | `allocate_engram()` returns `NVLinkEngramBuffer` when the flag is on |
| `deepinfer/model_executor/models/v4_modules/engram.py` | In NVLink mode, `initialize()` passes the host shards instead of CUDA views of them |
| `tests/distributed/test_engram_nvlink.py` | **New.** 2-GPU `ci` test (skipped with fewer GPUs) |

### How the fetch works

1. **`write`**
   - Each rank keeps its shard in pinned host memory and reads it through UVA. With `DEEPINFER_ENGRAM_FORCE_GPU_STORAGE`, the shard is kept on the GPU instead.
   - The full FP8 scale table is kept on the GPU, about 6 GB per rank for V4.1.
2. **`fetch`**
   - Indices are padded to `max_num_tokens` and all-gathered.
   - Each rank `index_select`s the rows it owns and zero-fills the rest.
   - One `all_to_all_single` returns the rows to the requesting ranks.
   - Each rank selects rows by owner rank.
   - Output matches DeepEP: `[T, E·H]` rows, plus scales in the TMA-aligned (4) column-major layout.
3. **No host sync.** The fetch is captured by the existing CUDA graphs.

**Trade-off:** this is a collective, not a one-sided get. Every fetch moves `max_num_tokens`-padded buffers over NVLink and needs all ranks to take part. It aims to make these nodes work, not to match GIN performance.

## Usage

```bash
export EP_DISABLE_GIN=1   # also enables DEEPINFER_ENGRAM_NVLINK_FETCH
python examples/offline_inference.py --ep 4
```

## Testing

Setup: one node, 4× B200, NVLink, GIN unavailable, driver 580.178, CUDA 13.1, torch 2.13.0+cu132, NCCL 2.32.3.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruff check --no-cache` / `ruff format --check --no-cache` | ✅ |
| `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_nvlink.py` (2 GPUs) | ✅ 1 passed. FP8 rows and scales are byte-identical to a direct full-table lookup, with ragged token counts across ranks (64 / 1 / 7–8 / 32–33) and the expected scale strides |
| `examples/offline_inference.py --ep 4` before this PR (`EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`) | ❌ illegal address in the first forward |
| `examples/offline_inference.py --ep 4` **with this PR** | ✅ Completes with 50/50 samples. Profile run, KV-cache init, warm-up and CUDA graph capture all pass. Outputs are identical across DP ranks |

Note: on this host, NCCL's NVLS multicast setup intermittently fails with `Cuda failure 999` in `ncclMcGroupBuildPartitions`, independent of this change. The unit test was run with `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`.

Sample outputs (DP 0):

| # | Prompt | Output | tokens | accept | decode_ppl |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 中国的首都是哪里？ | 北京 … | 96 | 53% | 1.1832 |
| 1 | Who wrote Romeo and Juliet? | William Shakespeare … | 104 | 51% | 1.0850 |
| 2 | 1 image: carrot color | Orange … | 128 | 47% | 1.3260 |
| 3 | 3 images | Carrots … | 34 | 32% | 1.4925 |
| 4 | 5-image 4-shot | `4\n\nRelated questions` ⚠️ | 5 | 0% | 2.0001 |

## ⚠️ Open questions

- **Decode PPL does not match `tests/models/offline_decode_ppl.json`**, and sample 4's answer is wrong. The run differs from the golden setup in more than this change:
  - **Checkpoint:** local `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (snapshot `dba1be0a`) vs the default `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`.
  - **Parallel config:** EP4 / CP1 / DP4 vs the golden's EP4 / CP2 / DP2.
  - **This change:** Engram over NVLink. MLOPart was also unavailable on this host.

  None of these has been isolated yet. I don't have a GIN-capable node for an A/B against the native path, so a check from someone who does would be very helpful. I also plan to run GSM8K next.
- **Performance is not measured yet.** The only end-to-end run was the first one and included JIT compilation.
- **Better design?** On a single node, a one-sided alternative is possible: put the whole table in shared, `cudaHostRegister`ed host memory and read the needed rows through UVA. That avoids both the collectives and the padding. I'd welcome maintainer input on which direction you prefer.
